statement: Truncated copies are under-counted. The audit reports 7 INCOMPLETE_COPY_TRUNCATED files, but 19 raw judgment files have no %%EOF anywhere and 41 have none in the last 2 KB. The audit flags a file as truncated only if PyMuPDF also fails to open it; pdf_eof_marker is recorded in the batches and never used. At least 8 of the extra files are missing their later pages (text on pp.1-16 of 34, 1-76 of 171, 1-83 of 171, 1-7 of 32, 1-4 of 32, 1-5 of 32, 1-3 of 8, 1-15 of 28) yet are counted PROCESSED and labelled PARTIAL_TEXT_LAYER / 'scanned pages need OCR'. OCR cannot recover them; they need re-acquisition. None is in CONTINUATION_MANIFEST.csv.

requested_action: Add a disposition for 'opens but no trailing %%EOF' (page-count vs pages-with-text), list those files in the continuation manifest as needing a complete copy, and correct the summary identity (processed-complete vs processed-from-incomplete copy).

statement: The persisted batches are not reproducible from the committed extractor. Re-running extraction with the committed tools gives byte-identical output for batches 4-19 but different output for batches 0-3 (800 files): 242 files gain case numbers in case_numbers_text_p1_3. Batches 0-3 were produced by an earlier case-number pattern under the same EXTRACTOR_VERSION 'c10-jextract/5', and the resume check compares only the version string and the input list, so they were skipped. 'assemble --check' cannot detect this because it rebuilds from the batches. Effect: about 157 metadata records would move to MATCH and about 38 from NOT_FOUND_IN_TEXT to NOT_CONFIRMED_IN_TEXT (approximate; my status function is a close re-implementation). The published case-number counts (MATCH 3038 / NOT_CONFIRMED 372 / NOT_FOUND 413) therefore mix two extractor behaviours, and jextract.py's statement that a rerun gives identical results is not true for these four batches.
evidence: rev_ws/rerun_all_batches.log; rev_ws/stale_batches_0_3_diff.csv; sample S05 (CWP-26686-2025 printed on p.1, reported NOT_FOUND_IN_TEXT)
requested_action: Regenerate batches 0-3 and reassemble; key the resume check on a hash of jextract.py (or bump the version on every pattern change); add a check mode that re-extracts a sample of batches.

statement: C10-QP-02 names the wrong file. The proposal says to register a separate India Code compilation source 'with candidate copy d163e785...' and in the same sentence says 'the second India Code file d163e785 ... is not identified and is not proposed'. d163e785 is the 40.9 MB Hindi text in Gazette pagination (confirmed on the page image); the compilation is d4449e99 (a2023-45.pdf). The builder takes cands[0], which sorts d163e785 first. The same mislabel is in the evidence text of the 12 BNS citation rows ('d163e785bfb3: ... India Code compilation (as on 06-10-2025)'). QUALITY_C10_FINDINGS.md states the intended hash (d4449e99), so the prose and the CSV disagree, and the quality workstream calls d163e785 unidentified while the statutory workstream identifies it.
evidence: quality/outputs/proposals_c10.csv row C10-QP-02; build_quality_c10.py lines 759-764; citation_coverage_c10.csv row C10Q-CW-0807; statutory/registration_proposals_c10.csv rows d163e785 and d4449e99; raw_manifest original_filename Hh202345.pdf vs a2023-45.pdf
requested_action: Select the candidate by identity, not sort order; correct QP-02 and the 12 evidence strings; align with the statutory identification.

statement: Outcome candidates are also unreliable on ordinary High Court orders, and the audit does not surface the disagreement it already holds. In my random sample of 20 non-reviewed judgments the outcome candidate was right in 12, wrong in 3 and missed in 4 (1 not applicable). All 3 wrong ones took 'pending applications stand disposed of' as the result of a petition that was dismissed or allowed. Corpus-wide, crawler outcome and text candidate disagree in 549 of the 1,775 records that have both (349 are dismissed-vs-disposed), and the contradictions column is empty for those rows. Where they disagreed in my sample the crawler metadata was right 3 times out of 4. The summary reports outcome reliability only from the 30-judgment high-risk sample.
evidence: rev_ws/fable_review_ws_3257ebb9_sample20.csv (S04, S05, S12 wrong; S01, S11, S13, S16 missed; S09 metadata wrong); HF_JUDGMENT_METADATA_AUDIT.csv outcome_meta vs outcome_text_candidate
requested_action: Flag outcome disagreement in the contradictions column and the queue; skip 'pending/miscellaneous application(s) ... disposed of' sentences; add the ordinary-judgment measurement to the summary.
